catastrophe.name: The Fracture
catastrophe.cause: Nuclear war shattered Earth into floating islands.

geography.landform: Fractured continents and floating rock islands above an atmospheric void
geography.boundaries: Map labels mark regions of influence, not surveyed borders.

magnetic_fields.behavior: Erratic and turbulent in motion, but their patterns are predictable.
magnetic_fields.navigation: Ships use magnetic motors to travel through the fields between cities and mining sites.

humanity.adaptation: Survivors evolved over generations under the influence of the magnetic fields.

gravity_and_energy.city_support: Magneton technology stabilizes floating cities and islands, preventing them from falling.
gravity_and_energy.local_gravity: Generated local fields reproduce the experience of the old Earth’s gravity.
gravity_and_energy.power: Oppositely polarized metal components move in magnetic motors, powering city and transport systems.
gravity_and_energy.fictional_physics: These are rules of the setting; no real-world scientific mechanism is established.

properties: Most malleable of the Magneton types
Impenetrable and impervious to any weapons

visual_concept.appearance: Chief engineer: middle-aged human woman, grey hair tied back, round goggles on forehead, crimson work shirt, brown leather apron, practical gloves. Other engineers wear simple workshop clothes, no silver armour.

Human civilians of varied ages and backgrounds in practical, prosperous city clothes: market workers, families and merchants. Fear, confusion and urgent movement; no silver armour. No graphic injuries.

After the two-front campaign, Serendipity holds the main dock but Ironveil schooners intercept ore carriers. Four owned capitals remain. Council naval captains wear navy/crimson, never Type C armour. Rovan offers paid service to local pilots; no acceptance or new territorial outcome is established.
Exactly FOUR owned capital ships still. Show no capital ship in these council/workshop scenes. Serendipity holds the main dock; ore routes remain vulnerable.
Naval captains are ordinary navy/crimson officers, not five silver knights. Rovan’s streak/beard, Tomas’s square glasses, Mara’s long braid and Idris’s curls/beard remain recognisable.
Paid-service offer is voluntary and UNANSWERED. No allegiance accepted, new victory, ship loss or territorial change.
Chronological cuts between dispatch, workshop and a later council; no invented exact elapsed travel times.

PURPOSE: Regenerate ONE comic illustration for FIXED holder 462.00 by 400.00 logical pixels, aspect 1.1550:1. LANDSCAPE. Requested output 1104x960. Do NOT resize or redesign the holder. Paint a NEW composition for it, not a framed photo.

SCENE: Single continuous Oram repair workshop: foreground one female engineer in practical brown apron and rolled sleeves studies a stalled open magnetic engine, a FEW bronze Type A offcuts and faint green Type B components on bench, empty material trays, unfinished pipes and idle tools. Behind her through wide open doorway, ordinary repair workers queue at a pay desk where a clerk shows a nearly empty coin tray, no payment being handed out. Worried waiting workers and unfinished reconstruction; no power outage catastrophe established. Small crimson/SILVER Veymarch flag on pay desk. No silver Type C suit, no crystal armour, no ships. Portrait-ish layout, all important faces and machinery above bottom narration.
CAMERA: Use a clear, tightly composed shot with the important action filling the aperture; do not copy the old wide framing.

STYLE: Magneton graphic novel: painted ink, tactile bronze machinery, silver Type C, crimson Veymarch cloth, navy/gold Auric Reach uniforms; atmospheric floating islands. Consistent with supplied scene references, not photorealistic.
